source.title_on_document: A Comparative Study on the Impact of AIGC and Traditional Inspiration Sources on the Design Process of Designers

paper_design_summary: Twelve design master's students were split into a Pinterest (traditional image search) group and a Midjourney (AIGC) group of six each. Each participant did two 20-minute brainstorming tasks, one low-constraint and one high-constraint, while thinking aloud, followed by a semi-structured interview. The paper analyzes the inspiration process (keywords entered, search behavior, images selected) qualitatively and with simple counts; no creativity or diversity score of the design output is reported.

studies.label: Think-aloud ideation study (Midjourney vs Pinterest, low and high task constraint)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Inspiration source: Pinterest (traditional search engine) or Midjourney (AIGC); every participant did both a low-constraint and a high-constraint task
assignment.quote: The experiment is divided into a traditional search engine group (using Pinterest, n = 6) and an AIGC group (using Midjourney, n = 6). Both groups conduct brainstorming activities under two different levels of task constraints, namely high and low.

arms.name: Traditional search engine
arms.description: Pinterest as inspiration source during two 20-minute brainstorming tasks

arms.name: AIGC
arms.description: Midjourney as inspiration source during two 20-minute brainstorming tasks

participants.exclusions: None reported. The paper gives 12 participants and group sizes of 6 and 6; it does not say how participants were allocated to groups.
participants.who: Master's students from the design school (7 female, 5 male, average age 23, 4-5 years of design learning experience)
participants.country: not_stated (authors' affiliation: School of Design, Hunan University, China)
participants.quote: The participants are 12 master's students from the design school, including 7 females and 5 males, with an average age of 23 years old, and all have 4-5 years of design learning experience.

ai_tool.how_used: Participants entered keywords to generate images as inspiration for design ideation; the comparison group searched Pinterest for images.

task.description: Design ideation brainstorming under a low-constraint task (conceptual design of Mars survival) and a high-constraint task (car cabin/interior sleep design, per keywords in Figure 3), each followed by a 5-minute review, then an interview
task.duration: 20 minutes per task plus 5-minute review each; 5-minute intro; interview 15-20 minutes in Figure 1 (20-30 minutes in text)

outcomes.name: Number of inspiration images selected
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Pooled count of inspiration-related images selected per condition during the inspiration selection phase; a process measure, not a score of the design output

contrasts.reported: users of traditional search engines chose 241 inspiration-related images, whereas AIGC users selected only 76 (no test reported)

outcomes.name: Commonality of search keywords across participants
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Descriptive word clouds of keywords entered by participants (directly related, extended subject, extended style words), by condition and task constraint; scored on search inputs, not on design outputs; no numeric measure

contrasts.reported: Low constraint: with AIGC 'there was no significant commonality in the main subject words', but style words such as 'technology' and 'minimalism' were chosen by multiple participants and did not appear with search engines. High constraint with AIGC: 'there is no longer a commonality among participants in the selection of extended style words.' No statistics.

eligibility.reason: Twelve participants (6 Midjourney, 6 Pinterest), below the 50-person threshold (PDF p. 3, printed p. 105, Method). Design is other: two-group comparative experiment; assignment not stated. Neither the methods text nor Figure 1 describes how participants were allocated, so neither random nor nonrandom assignment is established; quasi_people requires nonrandom assignment (PDF p. 3, printed p. 105, Method and Figure 1; form-spec.md, Field notes, design_class). The outcomes concern search keywords, search behavior, and selected inspiration images; no creativity or diversity score is reported for participant-produced design output (PDF pp. 3-9, printed pp. 105-111, Results and Conclusion). The study does not qualify for core or context inclusion and belongs in the screening report only.

one_line_finding: With 12 design students, Midjourney users selected fewer inspiration images than Pinterest users (76 vs 241, p. 108) and searched more deeply and iteratively, per qualitative think-aloud analysis; no creativity score of the output is reported.
